links.outcome: Discrimination deterioration of EMR prediction models over time under temporal dataset shift
links.effect: Across three clinical prediction tasks, model discrimination deteriorated over time; pathophysiological features helped mitigate this deterioration. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
links.quote: We investigate three standard clinical prediction tasks and find that while feature contributions to initial performance differ across tasks, pathophysiological features help mitigate temporal discrimination deterioration.

unlisted_practices: Building predictive models from pathophysiological EMR feature categories to improve robustness to temporal dataset shift
Using Shapley-value attribution of feature groups and categories to explain contributions to sustained model performance

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates how selecting pathophysiological vs healthcare process feature groups impacts model robustness and mitigates performance deterioration under temporal dataset shift.

primary.practice: feature selection based on pathophysiological vs process categories to mitigate temporal dataset shift
